newsitem.title: ITALY: Blast causes first death in Albania security force.
newsitem.headline: Blast causes first death in Albania security force.

text.p: A 19-year-old soldier serving with an Italian-led multinational security force in Albania died on Wednesday when an explosive device he was handling went off, defence ministry officials said.
The dead soldier, Corporal Diego Vaira from Fossano, Italy, was the first casualty from the 7,000-strong force.
Three Italian military personnel were injured in the 9 a.m. (0700 GMT) incident in a store tent at a field hospital near the southern Albanian port of Vlore.
Italian Defence Ministry undersecretary Massimo Brutti said the death was apparently not the result of an attack by armed Albanians or a stray bullet. He had no further details.
Vlore was the cradle of an insurrection that swept Albania earlier this year after many thousands lost their life savings in the collapse of shady pyramid savings schemes.

The popular uprising triggered a breakdown in law and order and a Multinational Protection Force arrived in April to help restore it and pave the way for elections, which were carried out successfully on June 29 and July 6.
A defence ministry spokesman said an inquiry was under way into Wednesday's explosion. He said Vaira had not been a professional soldier and went to Albania with a sanitary team.
Marshal Francesco Seminara, 36, suffered injuries to his left hand and may need to have a finger amputated. He was being airlifted to the southern Italian port of Brindisi.

Corporal Paolo Spagnolo, 24, suffered slight wounds to his left arm and Corporal Sergio Chiaramello, 20, light injuries all over his body. The men worked at the field hospital as sanitary assistant and electrician.
Military sources said the device which exploded was not Italian-made and not part of Italian military equipment.
"We are wounded, perturbed, and express our great condolences and anguish for a life which has been lost," Brutti told reporters on the margins of a conference in Rome.
"I would like to express our gratitude to the Italian soldiers for their work carried out in conditions of great difficulty," he said.
Italy's lower house of parliament observed a minute's silence on Wednesday.

Carlo Rognoni, vice-chairman of the upper Senate, called the death a "tribute of blood that we pay for the pacification of Albania and which leaves us distressed but also proud for what our soldiers are doing".
Italy, which has contributed the greatest number of soldiers to the multinational force, had originally not planned to send non-professional soldiers but had been forced to do so to make up numbers.
Some 300-400 men were sent to Albania for logistical duties.
